senses.gloss: (b. h.; √בז to tread, v. בּוּז) to tread upon, whence to despise, spurn, degrade. Ab. d’R. Nath. ch. XXIX הבּוֹזֶה את חבירו וכ׳ he who spurns his neighbor (rebuking him) for a sacred cause. Ib. הן בּוֹזִין בעצמן they make themselves contemptible (neglecting their appearance). Part. pass. בָּזוּי, f. בְּזוּיָה.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 5:6:3">Y. Sot. V, end, 20ᵈ</cite> <he>שהיתה נבואתו ב׳</he> his prophetic gift was degraded (by him). Ruth. R. to I, 1 <he>מי שהוא ב׳ בדבריו</he> he who becomes contemptible through his own words (in not practicing what he teaches).

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 6:5">Cant. R. to VI, 5</cite> <he>מה עז זו ב׳</he> as the goat is despised <he>כך בְּזוּיִין וכ׳</he> so were the Israelites made despicable at Shittim (through debauchery); a. fr.

senses.gloss: <cite ref="B00433">same</cite>. Ab. d’R. Nath. l. c. Y. Sot. l. c. he (Isaac) is called Buzi, <he>שבי׳ את וכ׳</he> because he made all idolatrous temples appear contemptible (by his willingness to be sacrificed to the Lord).
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 30:7">Gen. R. s. 30</cite> (play on <cite ref="B00220"><he>בוז</he></cite> <cite ref="Job 12:5">Job XII, 5</cite>) <he>שהיו מְבַזִּים עליו</he> they sneered at him.
Aboth III, 11 המְבַזֶּה את וכ׳ he who disregards the festive weeks (treating them as week days); a. fr.—Part. Pu. מְבוּזֶּה, pl. מְבוּזִּין.

<cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 3:3">Ab. Zar. III, 3</cite> <he>המב׳</he> common vessels, opp. <he>מכובדין</he> ornamental; <cite ref="Tosefta Avodah Zarah 5:1">Tosef. ib. V</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Avodah Zarah 6:1">VI</cite>), 1 <he>בזויין</he> ed. Zuck. (Var. <he>מב׳</he>); Y. ib. III, 42ᵈ; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be despised, humbled, exposed. Y. Taan. II, beg. 65ᵃ you cannot compare המִתְבַּזֶּה מעצמו וכ׳ one who humbles himself to one who is humbled by others.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 97b">Keth. 97ᵇ</cite>. Ruth. R. to I, 1 <he>אימתי ד״ת מִתְבַּזִּין וכ׳</he> when are the words of the Law despised by the people? When the scholars make them contemptible (through their conduct); a. fr.
